emuni.intro: An intergovernmental university on the Slovenian coast, founded as a joint project of the Euro-Mediterranean Partnership countries. Teaching is in English, within a network of partner universities across the Mediterranean.
emuni.reputation: Since its founding, EMUNI has focused on the social and natural sciences with an emphasis on sustainable development and international cooperation. Master's and doctoral programmes cover intercultural business communication, digitalisation and human rights, kinesiology and sport sciences, with specialisations in the green economy, project management and international law. Partnerships with institutions and companies across Europe open the door to real projects and internships.
highlights: A university of the Euro-Mediterranean Partnership — partner institutions in dozens of countries
Fully taught in English, with no Slovenian language requirement
Interdisciplinary programmes: sustainable development, human rights, kinesiology
HALS summer school in Piran and Koper, worth 3 ECTS credits
emuni.campus: The university sits on Slovenia's Adriatic coast, in Piran and Portorož — towns with a Mediterranean climate and a high quality of life. Students choose between halls of residence and private accommodation near campus, at roughly 300 to 500 euros a month. Living costs in Slovenia are noticeably lower than in Western Europe, and food is varied and affordable.
emuni.admissions: Applications are accepted in three rounds, the main ones in June and September. A master's application requires a bachelor's degree worth at least 180 ECTS credits; doctoral applicants also submit a master's degree and proof of recognition of prior education. Master's tuition is 4,900–5,800 euros per year and doctoral studies 5,800 euros. EMUNI awards scholarships based on academic results and holds regular information sessions for prospective students.
documents: Degree certificate and academic transcript from the previous level of study
Proof of English proficiency (B2 or C1)
Translations of documents and proof of recognition of a foreign degree
Copy of passport or ID card
emuni.metaDescription: EMUNI University, Piran and Koper: an intergovernmental university on the Slovenian coast, taught in English. Degrees, tuition and deadlines.

metu.intro: Hungary's largest private university, in the heart of Budapest. It brings business, social sciences and the arts together through interdisciplinary modules and project work, taught entirely in English.
metu.reputation: The QS Stars system awarded the university four stars out of five, and a maximum five for internationalisation. METU is best known for its creative programmes — animation, media, design and photography — and for the collaboration of its art and design institutes with festivals, studios and the creative industries. Its myBRAND programme is recognised as an educational innovation because it develops a student's professional profile, not just academic knowledge.
highlights: Four QS stars, and five stars for internationalisation
The region's strongest creative programmes: animation, design, media production
Interdisciplinary modules — business and the arts in one curriculum
The myBRAND programme for professional development and personal branding
metu.campus: The campus is in Budapest, with easy access to everything the city offers. The university runs its own halls of residence, the most affordable option in the early years at around 270 to 440 euros a month; private flats range from 500 to 600 euros. Students eat in the campus canteens or in nearby restaurants and cafés, with another 150 to 250 euros a month covering all remaining costs.
metu.admissions: METU admits students in autumn and spring intakes. The early deadline for the autumn intake is usually mid-September, while the final deadline for the spring intake for non-EU students can fall in November. The university offers discounts for new applicants and scholarships for students with excellent results, which can significantly reduce tuition.
documents: Secondary school certificates and diploma (for bachelor's programmes)
Bachelor's degree (for master's and MBA programmes)
Proof of English proficiency (IELTS, TOEFL or equivalent)
metu.metaDescription: Budapest Metropolitan University: film, design, tourism and business taught in English in Budapest. Tuition, scholarships and 2026 deadlines.

aydin.intro: One of Turkey's most respected private universities, on the European side of Istanbul. Over 40,000 students, including more than 4,000 international students from over 100 countries.
aydin.reputation: Founded in 2007, Istanbul Aydin University grew quickly into a leading private institution and ranks highly in the QS EECA rankings for Eastern Europe and Central Asia. The university works with over 450 universities worldwide through Erasmus+ and bilateral agreements, giving students the option of an exchange or part of their degree in another country.
highlights: Over 40,000 students, 4,000+ international students from more than 100 countries
Partnerships with 450+ universities through Erasmus+ and bilateral agreements
A modern campus in Florya, close to the airport and the coast
Six intakes a year — no need to wait for September
aydin.campus: The Florya campus is equipped with modern laboratories, a library, research centres, sports facilities, restaurants and cafés. Its location gives quick access to the metro and to Istanbul's landmarks. Halls of residence cost 150 to 300 euros a month and total living costs average 300 to 500 euros. The university helps students find accommodation near campus.
aydin.admissions: Students can enrol in six intakes a year — spring, summer and autumn, each in two sessions. Applications are accepted year-round, but documents should be submitted at least 30 days before the chosen start date. Applicants who need a visa should apply several months earlier. Tuition for English-taught bachelor's programmes is 3,000–6,000 euros per year, and 3,000–5,000 euros in total for a master's.
documents: Proof of language proficiency (IELTS, TOEFL or Duolingo; TÖMER for Turkish)
aydin.metaDescription: Istanbul Aydin University: 40,000+ students from over 100 countries and six intakes a year. Programmes, tuition and living costs in Istanbul.

nicosia.intro: The largest private university in Cyprus, with campuses in Nicosia and Athens. Students from over 100 countries, teaching in English and internationally recognised degrees.
nicosia.reputation: Founded in 1980, UNIC is known for its innovation and global outlook — particularly in medicine, business, IT and law. It was the first university in the world to launch a master's in blockchain and digital currency, and today offers over 80 master's and 20 doctoral programmes, many of them fully online. In-demand fields include cyber security, the metaverse, energy and healthcare.
highlights: The world's first master's degree in blockchain and digital currency
Over 80 master's and 20 doctoral programmes, many fully online
Its own premium residences: SIX, U and TRIANGLE
Scholarships covering 50 to 80 percent of tuition
nicosia.campus: The main campus is in the Engomi district of Nicosia — an urban complex of over 20 buildings with modern classrooms, laboratories, libraries and sports facilities, surrounded by more than 70 restaurants and cafés in a pedestrian zone. The university also runs its own residences with studio apartments, a gym, study rooms and 24/7 security, at 350 to 600 euros a month. Private accommodation starts at 300 to 500 euros.
nicosia.admissions: The two main intakes are September/October and February/March, and most programmes operate rolling admissions. Early applications automatically improve scholarship chances — merit awards reach 50 to 80 percent of tuition, and up to 100 percent for exceptional candidates. There are also sports scholarships of up to 40 percent and need-based support for students from the Balkans. Non-EU applicants should apply three to four months ahead for the visa process.
documents: Bachelor's or master's degree with academic transcript
Statement of purpose (with a research proposal for doctoral applicants)
Two to three letters of recommendation
Proof of English proficiency (IELTS 6.5+ or TOEFL iBT 79+)
nicosia.metaDescription: University of Nicosia, Cyprus: over 80 master's programmes and the world's first blockchain master's. Tuition, scholarships and deadlines. Free assessment.

ais.intro: A private international business school in La Tour-de-Peilz, on the shore of Lake Geneva. It combines the American education system with Swiss standards and students from over 60 countries.
ais.reputation: The school has been running for more than 30 years and ranks in the top four in Switzerland on the QS list, placing in the global top 150–200 for its master's in management. It is accredited by IACBE, and partnerships with IATA, IBM and Apple allow professional certifications to be built into the degree. A dual degree with Tiffin University in the United States means two diplomas from one programme.
highlights: Dual degree with Tiffin University (USA) — two diplomas from one programme
Top 4 in Switzerland in the QS rankings
IATA, IBM and Apple professional certifications built into the curriculum
Internships at Nestlé, Hublot, the UN and the IOC — all near campus
ais.campus: The campus is on the Swiss Riviera, on the shore of Lake Geneva near Lausanne — modern, with interactive classrooms, a library, computer labs and a snack bar. Small classes and personal mentors are part of the approach, and student clubs, excursions and sport round out the teaching. University residences start at 750 francs a month; food, transport and mandatory health insurance add 800 to 1,500 francs.
ais.admissions: Admissions are rolling, with main intakes in October and February. Non-EU students should apply 10 to 12 weeks ahead for the visa. Tuition is 18,000–25,000 francs per year for bachelor's programmes and 16,000–25,000 francs in total for a master's, plus an application fee and admission fee. Payment in instalments is possible, and merit scholarships offer 20 to 30 percent off.
documents: Certified secondary school or bachelor's degree
Proof of English proficiency (IELTS 6.0+, TOEFL or equivalent)
ais.metaDescription: American Institute of Applied Sciences: an American-Swiss business degree by Lake Geneva, with a dual diploma. Tuition, deadlines and entry rules.

cbs.intro: One of Germany's leading business schools, with its main campus in Cologne and students from over 75 countries. Teaching is in English, with the emphasis on practice — case studies, projects and work with companies.
cbs.reputation: CBS was founded in 1993 as a private university of applied sciences and is accredited by FIBAA, IACBE and the German Science Council. It ranks among the best private business schools in Germany according to WirtschaftsWoche. Its network covers over 120 partner universities and companies, and compulsory internships plus a careers centre keep employment rates high.
highlights: FIBAA, IACBE and Wissenschaftsrat accreditations
Over 120 partner universities and companies
A compulsory internship in every programme
The semester fee includes free public transport
cbs.campus: The main campus is in Cologne's Rodenkirchen district on the banks of the Rhine, with further campuses in Mainz near Frankfurt and Potsdam near Berlin. Campuses have modern classrooms, libraries, IT centres and group work spaces. The school reserves places in student residences and helps through its Accommodation Office — housing costs 400 to 800 euros a month and total living costs 800 to 1,200 euros. The Cologne cafeteria serves meals at student prices.
cbs.admissions: Admissions are rolling, with no strict final deadlines. The autumn semester starts in October and the spring semester in March or April; non-EU applicants should apply three to four months earlier for the visa. Tuition is 7,290–8,000 euros per semester for bachelor's and 7,500–9,000 euros for master's programmes, plus a semester fee of around 300 euros. Scholarships offer 10 to 30 percent off.
documents: Secondary school or bachelor's degree with certified translation
Proof of English proficiency (IELTS 6.5+ or TOEFL iBT 83+)
cbs.metaDescription: CBS International Business School, Cologne: a German business school with compulsory placements. English-taught degrees, tuition and deadlines.

eubs.intro: A business school with campuses in Barcelona, Geneva and Munich, plus a digital campus as a flexible option. Programmes run from bachelor's to MBA and doctoral level, all in English.
eubs.reputation: EU Business School holds four QS stars for excellence in business education, and its online MBA has topped the CEO Magazine Online Global Rankings for several consecutive years. The school is strongly international — a significant share of students come from abroad, and moving between campuses and online components is possible during your studies.
highlights: Online MBA ranked #1 in the CEO Magazine Online Global Rankings
Four QS stars for business education
Move between the Barcelona, Geneva and Munich campuses mid-degree
Teaching through case studies, company visits and simulations
eubs.campus: The campuses sit in prestigious European cities, and the cost of living varies considerably — Geneva is the most expensive, Barcelona and Munich more affordable. Accommodation in Barcelona is a significant expense: private flats cost more, shared housing noticeably less. Tuition depends above all on the campus: 7,050 euros per semester for the digital and Munich campuses, 13,800–15,100 francs for Montreux and Geneva.
eubs.admissions: Programmes have several start dates — in Barcelona these are typically October, February, and June or August for foundation and bridging programmes. The school offers merit scholarships and financial support for international students, and early applications often carry additional discounts. Details vary by campus and programme.
documents: Secondary school certificates and diploma (for bachelor's programmes)
Bachelor's degree (for master's and MBA programmes)
Proof of English proficiency (IELTS, TOEFL or equivalent)
eubs.metaDescription: EU Business School: Barcelona, Geneva and Munich, with the world's top-ranked online MBA. English-taught degrees, tuition by campus, deadlines.

ibs.intro: A private business school founded in Budapest in 1991, now also with campuses in Vienna and Dubai. Degrees are UK-accredited, in partnership with the University of Buckingham.
ibs.reputation: IBS is one of the most international business schools in the region — more than 60 percent of students come from abroad and teaching is exclusively in English. Through the partnership with the University of Buckingham, students earn a British degree that is highly valued worldwide. The school was among the first in Central Europe to introduce data analytics and digital marketing degrees in cooperation with leading IT companies.
highlights: A British degree through the University of Buckingham partnership
Three campuses to choose from: Budapest, Vienna and Dubai
Over 60 percent of students come from abroad
Among the first in the region to offer data analytics degrees
ibs.campus: All campuses are in urban districts with easy access to cultural events and business centres. IBS has an on-campus residence in Budapest and works with agencies and residences that specialise in international students in all three cities. Student hostels cost 250 to 500 euros a month, private flats 300 to 600 euros in Budapest and Vienna and 500 to 800 euros in Dubai. Food and transport add 200 to 400 euros.
ibs.admissions: There are two intakes a year — September and February — on all campuses. Early applications by 31 March or 30 September bring discounts and priority for scholarships worth up to 50 percent of tuition. Final deadlines are 15 July and 15 December. Applicants who need a visa should apply at least three months ahead.
documents: Proof of English proficiency (IELTS, TOEFL or Duolingo, minimum B2)
ibs.metaDescription: International Business School: a British degree in Budapest, Vienna or Dubai. English-taught programmes, tuition, scholarships and deadlines.

wittenborg.intro: A university of applied sciences in Apeldoorn, in the heart of the Netherlands, with over 1,200 students from more than 100 countries. Teaching is 100 percent in English.
wittenborg.reputation: Founded in 1987, Wittenborg is one of the most international universities in the Netherlands. It is accredited by NVAO in the Netherlands and by FIBAA, which makes its degrees internationally recognised. The focus is on business, management, entrepreneurship, tourism, IT and sustainability, and every student has the option of a work placement with an international company during their studies.
highlights: Six intakes a year — studies begin roughly every two months
NVAO (Netherlands) and FIBAA accreditation
Students from over 100 countries, teaching 100 percent in English
Work placements with international companies during your degree
wittenborg.campus: The main campus is in Apeldoorn, a quiet and safe city, and the university also has campuses in Amsterdam and Munich. The Apeldoorn campus is modern, with classrooms, seminar rooms, a library and student spaces, and restaurants, shops and sports centres nearby. The university helps with finding housing: student residences and shared flats cost 400 to 650 euros a month, with total living costs of 800 to 1,100 euros.
wittenborg.admissions: The admissions system is unusually flexible — studies can begin six times a year, so there is no waiting for September. Non-EU students should apply two to three months before their intended start date for the visa process. Tuition is 9,800 euros per year for bachelor's programmes and 13,300 euros in total for a master's. Available scholarships include the Wittenborg Holland Scholarship, the Orange Tulip Scholarship and partial merit awards.
documents: Proof of English proficiency (IELTS 6.0+, TOEFL iBT 80+ or Duolingo 95+)
Certified translations of all documents not in English
wittenborg.metaDescription: Wittenborg University, Netherlands: six intakes a year and placements with international companies. English-taught degrees, tuition and costs.

ucam.intro: A private Catholic university in Murcia, known as Spain's sports university. Small classes, compulsory work placements and students from over 115 countries.
ucam.reputation: Over 90 percent of UCAM graduates find work or continue their studies within 12 months, with average salaries above the national level. The university entered the QS World University Rankings for the first time in 2026 and holds five QS stars for teaching, inclusiveness and employability. It sponsors over 20 professional teams and counts Olympic champions among its students, and is equally strong in the health sciences — dentistry, physiotherapy and nutrition.
highlights: Five QS stars; over 90 percent of graduates employed within a year
Spain's sports university — 20+ sponsored professional teams
An 18th-century monastery campus, Los Jerónimos, a national monument
Collaboration with institutions such as Stanford and the University of Bologna
ucam.campus: The main Los Jerónimos campus occupies an 18th-century monastery declared a national historic and artistic monument, and the university also has campuses in Cartagena and Madrid. Murcia is a sunny Mediterranean city with over 3,000 hours of sunshine a year and the beaches of the Costa Cálida close by. UCAM has no halls of its own but offers residences, shared flats and rooms through its Accommodation Service — 300 to 600 euros a month, with total living costs of 600 to 1,000 euros.
ucam.admissions: Applications are rolling, with recommended intakes in September/October and sometimes February. The final deadline for English-taught bachelor's programmes is usually 31 July and 31 August for master's. Non-EU applicants should apply three to six months ahead for the visa and degree recognition. Bachelor's tuition ranges from 5,000 to 9,000 euros per year and master's from 8,000 to 12,000 euros in total.
documents: Secondary school or bachelor's degree with translation and legalisation
Academic transcripts and a copy of your passport
Proof of English proficiency (IELTS, TOEFL or Duolingo, minimum B2)
Letters of recommendation (for master's and MBA)
Degree recognition through the Spanish ministry (for non-EU applicants)
ucam.metaDescription: UCAM University, Murcia: Spain's sports and health sciences university. English-taught programmes, tuition, scholarships and 2026 deadlines.

fsm.intro: A foundation university in Istanbul's historic centre, with roots in 15th-century endowments. It combines Ottoman tradition with contemporary education and has over 8,000 students.
fsm.reputation: Founded in 2010 under the General Directorate of Foundations of Turkey, FSMVÜ is one of the few universities teaching in three languages — Turkish, English and Arabic. It is strongest in Islamic sciences, architecture and engineering. It is supported by a foundation dating from 1471, the oldest continuously operating educational endowment in the world, and its industry links and careers centre keep employment rates high.
highlights: Campuses in historic Ottoman buildings, including a Mimar Sinan complex
Teaching in three languages: Turkish, English and Arabic
Supported by a 1471 endowment — the world's oldest educational foundation
Up to 95 percent of students receive some form of tuition discount
fsm.campus: The university has several campuses in Istanbul's historic core — Topkapı, Haliç, Küçükayasofya, Validebağ, Kandilli and Yenikapı Mevlevihanesi — in Ottoman-era buildings renovated into modern classrooms, laboratories, libraries and sports centres. The city-centre location gives easy access to the Bosphorus and public transport. The university has no halls of its own but helps find private residences and shared flats from 400 dollars upwards.
fsm.admissions: The main autumn intake is in September, with applications from May to August, and some programmes also have a February spring intake. Admissions for international students are rolling, with early application recommended for the visa. Merit scholarships go up to 100 percent of tuition, and there are special provisions for students from the Balkans and for sporting achievement. Scholarship applications run alongside admission.
documents: Secondary school or bachelor's degree with certified translation
Proof of language proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS for English-taught programmes)
Motivation letter and CV (for master's and doctoral studies)
fsm.metaDescription: Fatih Sultan Mehmet University: campuses in Ottoman buildings in central Istanbul. Programmes, tuition from 2,000 USD and full scholarships.

aubg.intro: A prestigious private university in Blagoevgrad, at the foot of the Pirin mountains, offering American-style education in English. Founded in 1991.
aubg.reputation: AUBG is built on the American liberal arts college model — a broad choice of subjects, small classes, active student participation and an emphasis on critical thinking. Its degree is recognised in both the United States and the European Union, and its alumni network spans the region. The campus is modern and green, with halls of residence, libraries and sports fields, an hour's drive from Sofia.
highlights: American liberal arts model, with a degree recognised in the USA and the EU
A compact campus with halls, canteen and sports fields all in one place
Small-group teaching, in English
Summer programmes for ages 8 to 18+ — language, STEM and leadership
aubg.campus: The Blagoevgrad campus is surrounded by the Pirin and Rila mountains. The Skaptopara Residence Halls are on campus itself — comfortable rooms with Wi-Fi, a short walk from classes. Meals are served in the campus canteen, with healthy and vegetarian options, or in restaurants in town. Blagoevgrad is an affordable student city, and Sofia is about two hours away by bus or train.
aubg.admissions: AUBG admits students in the autumn intake, and early applications improve scholarship chances. Bachelor's tuition is around 6,700 euros per semester, and living costs in Blagoevgrad are among the lowest of any institution here — 500 to 900 euros a month. The university awards scholarships based on academic merit and financial need.
documents: Parental consent for under-18 summer programme participants
aubg.metaDescription: American University in Bulgaria, Blagoevgrad: an American liberal arts degree inside the EU, taught in English. Tuition, scholarships, deadlines.

jcu.intro: An American university in Rome, in the historic Trastevere district. Teaching in English, an international environment and small classes in one of Europe's most beautiful cities.
jcu.reputation: John Cabot University offers a broad range of liberal arts and social science programmes — economics, management and international business, communications, political science, art, history and psychology. The curriculum is built to global standards, which suits students interested in international cooperation, politics and culture. Alongside bachelor's degrees, master's programmes in art history and international affairs are available.
highlights: An American university in the heart of Rome, three campuses in Trastevere
A flexible curriculum with a wide choice of elective modules
Internships at embassies, international organisations and companies
Scholarships covering up to 50 percent of tuition
jcu.campus: Three campuses sit in Trastevere, one of Rome's most characterful districts, and include modern classrooms, art galleries, a library, computer labs and student residences. Students have access to canteens, student cafés and many restaurants nearby. Campus and private accommodation costs 700 to 1,200 euros a month, with living costs in Rome of 500 to 800 euros.
jcu.admissions: The autumn semester starts in September and the spring semester in January; applications are accepted year-round until places fill. JCU awards academic and financial scholarships covering up to 50 percent of tuition, with dedicated awards for students with excellent results and for candidates from the Balkans.
jcu.metaDescription: John Cabot University: an American university in Rome's Trastevere with 16 BA majors. Tuition, scholarships of up to 50% and entry deadlines.

gbsb.intro: A business school with campuses in Barcelona, Madrid and Malta, focused on digital business, innovation and entrepreneurship. Teaching is entirely in English.
gbsb.reputation: GBSB Global holds MFHEA accreditation from Malta, ASIC from the United Kingdom and ACBSP from the United States, and its Barcelona campus is registered in the Spanish RUCT system. The school holds a five-star QS rating for online study, employability and teaching quality. Its programmes connect business, technology and innovation, with an emphasis on digital transformation, sustainability and global leadership.
highlights: Five QS stars for online study, employability and teaching quality
MFHEA (Malta), ASIC (UK) and ACBSP (USA) accreditation
Three locations: Barcelona, Madrid and Malta
Specialisations from digital marketing to fashion and luxury
gbsb.campus: All campuses are in urban districts with easy access to business centres and cultural venues. The school has no halls of its own but works with agencies and residences for international students. Student residences cost 350 to 600 euros a month; private flats 450 to 700 euros in Barcelona and Madrid, or 350 to 550 euros in Malta. Food and transport add 250 to 350 euros, with noticeably lower prices in Malta.
gbsb.admissions: GBSB runs several intakes a year — most often October, January and April for the MBA and most master's programmes, while bachelor's degrees offer several start dates. Early applications in spring and early summer bring larger discounts and scholarships. Applicants who need a visa should apply two to three months ahead. Merit scholarships offer 15 to 30 percent off, alongside Women in Business and Leadership awards.
documents: Copy of passport and academic transcripts
Proof of English proficiency (IELTS 6.0, TOEFL iBT 72–80, Duolingo 95+ or interview)
gbsb.metaDescription: GBSB Global Business School: Barcelona, Madrid and Malta, focused on digital business. English-taught degrees, tuition, scholarships, deadlines.

bts.intro: An international school in Barcelona dedicated to technology and innovation. Master's programmes in computer science and digital business, with guaranteed internships through its network of partner companies.
bts.reputation: Barcelona Technology School brings in lecturers from industry and builds its programmes together with the technology sector. Its master's in digital solutions development is accredited by the University of Barcelona, and its big data solutions programme runs in partnership with Eurecat, Catalonia's largest technology centre. The school also covers user experience design and innovation in digital business.
highlights: Master's in digital solutions accredited by the University of Barcelona
Big data programme in partnership with Eurecat, Catalonia's technology centre
Guaranteed internships through a network of partner companies
Programmes run nine to twelve months
bts.campus: The school is in Barcelona — a city that combines a strong tech scene with beaches and a Mediterranean rhythm. Teaching happens in small groups, with the emphasis on real projects. Barcelona is one of Europe's most appealing cities for young people in technology, with an established startup community and a large number of international companies.
bts.admissions: Programmes start on set dates through the year, with applications accepted on a rolling basis until the cohort fills. The school awards scholarships to international students based on academic merit and financial need. Get in touch for exact deadlines, fees and entry requirements for the current year — we check them directly with the school.
documents: Degree certificate and academic transcript from previous studies
bts.metaDescription: Barcelona Technology School: master's degrees in computing and digital business, with guaranteed internships. Entry requirements and deadlines.

htl.intro: A specialist school in central Barcelona with over 15 years of experience in hospitality, tourism, business and languages. Every programme includes a compulsory paid internship.
htl.reputation: HTL ranks among the top ten European hospitality management schools for 2023 according to Higher Education Review, among the top ten most promising business schools in Spain for 2024 and among the top five in Europe for hotel management careers in 2025. It is accredited by the city councils of Barcelona, Madrid and Valencia, by the Spanish FUNDAE foundation and by Instituto Cervantes as a SIELE examination centre. Ninety-nine percent of students secure a paid placement.
highlights: 99 percent of students secure a paid internship
Top 10 European hospitality management schools (Higher Education Review)
An Instituto Cervantes centre for SIELE Spanish language exams
Four intakes a year and applications processed in three to four days
htl.campus: The campus is in central Barcelona, surrounded by beaches, restaurants, cafés and public transport. The school offers face-to-face teaching in modern classrooms alongside virtual and online options. It has no halls of its own but helps find residences, shared flats and apartments from 450 euros a month. Total monthly costs in Barcelona run from 900 to 1,200 euros.
htl.admissions: The school admits students four times a year — January, April, July and October for bachelor's and master's programmes. Applications close 30 days before the start date, with a limited number of places. Tuition is 6,000 euros per year for bachelor's programmes when paid in full, or 5,000 euros in total for a master's. Partial scholarships are awarded on the basis of results, motivation letter and an English test. The degrees are private, well suited to an industry career but not to further academic progression.
documents: Certificates or diploma from previous education
CV with work experience (for master's programmes)
Proof of English proficiency (IELTS 5.5+, TOEFL, Duolingo 75–80 or the school's own test)
Motivation letter (for master's programmes and scholarships)
htl.metaDescription: HTL University, Barcelona: hospitality and tourism with a compulsory paid internship. Four intakes a year, tuition and entry requirements. Free assessment.

mai.intro: One of Russia's leading universities in aviation, aeronautics, rocket technology and space engineering. Founded in 1930, with over 20,000 students.
mai.reputation: MAI is a key partner of the Russian aerospace industry, with links to Roscosmos and other manufacturers. The university is known for its more than 120 laboratories, its experimental factory and its own airfield. Teaching combines theory with industry projects and compulsory placements, and programmes are offered in both Russian and English, the latter aimed at international students.
highlights: Over 120 laboratories, an experimental factory and its own airfield
A direct partner of the Russian aerospace industry
Students from more than 50 countries
Halls of residence from just 70 to 100 dollars a month
mai.campus: The Moscow campus, near the Sokol, Voykovskaya and Shchukinskaya metro stations, works as a city within a city — modern classrooms, research centres, sports facilities and green space. Nine halls of residence with around 7,000 places offer block rooms for two to three people with a bathroom, kitchen, laundry and Wi-Fi, with priority given to international students. Campus canteens and cafés keep food costs low.
mai.admissions: Admissions are rolling, with main intakes in October and February. Non-EU students should apply 10 to 12 weeks ahead for the visa, with part of the tuition paid as a condition of the visa process. Tuition is 3,000 to 6,000 dollars per year, with English-taught programmes at the higher end. Merit scholarships offer 20 to 30 percent off.
documents: Secondary school or bachelor's degree with certified translation
Proof of language proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS, minimum B1–B2, or a Russian test)
Motivation letter and CV (for master's programmes)
mai.metaDescription: Moscow Aviation Institute: aviation, rocket technology and space engineering since 1930. English-taught degrees, tuition and cheap housing. Talk to us.

srh.intro: A private university of applied sciences with 18 campuses across Germany and over 200 programmes. Known for its CORE method — teaching without conventional lectures.
srh.reputation: SRH is among Germany's leading private universities for student satisfaction and holds five QS stars for online learning. The CORE approach — Competence Oriented Research and Education — replaces conventional lectures with small-group work, company projects and personal mentoring. Hackathons, startup labs and partnerships with companies such as SAP and BASF keep employability high.
highlights: The CORE method — project-based teaching instead of conventional lectures
Over 200 programmes across 18 campuses in Germany
Partnerships with companies such as SAP and BASF
Flexible formats: on campus, online or hybrid
srh.campus: Campuses are in Berlin, Heidelberg, Dresden, Hamburg, Cologne and other cities — Berlin as a cosmopolitan centre, Heidelberg as a green university town on the Neckar. All are equipped with classrooms, laboratories, libraries and student centres. The university helps find housing through partners: student residences and shared flats cost 400 to 800 euros a month, with total living costs of 800 to 1,200 euros.
srh.admissions: Admissions are rolling, with main intakes in October and April. Non-EU applicants should apply three to six months ahead for the visa. Tuition is 6,000–9,000 euros per semester for bachelor's and 6,500–9,000 euros for master's programmes, plus an enrolment fee and semester fee. Merit scholarships offer 30 to 50 percent off, alongside early bird, diversity and need-based awards.
documents: Degree from the previous level of study, certified and translated

kozminski.intro: A private business university in Warsaw, one of the most prestigious in Central and Eastern Europe. It holds the Triple Crown accreditations that only one percent of business schools worldwide have.
kozminski.reputation: Kozminski is the top private university in Poland in the Perspektywy 2025 ranking and 42nd in Europe in the Financial Times European Business Schools list. The Triple Crown — AACSB, EQUIS and AMBA — places it among the one percent of schools worldwide holding all three. Students come from over 70 countries, and 90 percent of graduates find work within six months.
highlights: Triple Crown accreditations: AACSB, EQUIS and AMBA
#1 private university in Poland, #42 in Europe per the Financial Times
90 percent of graduates employed within six months
Double degree programmes and Erasmus+ exchanges
kozminski.campus: The campus is in central Warsaw, on Jagiellońska street in the Praga Północ district — a modern complex with classrooms, libraries, sports fields and parking, close to the centre and public transport. The university helps with housing recommendations: private halls and shared flats cost 300 to 600 euros a month. Campus canteens and nearby cafés and shops keep food costs at 200 to 300 euros.
kozminski.admissions: Admissions are rolling — the main autumn intake is September/October, with applications by August for non-EU candidates, and the spring intake is in February with a January deadline. Tuition is 5,000–7,000 euros per year for bachelor's and 6,000–9,000 euros for master's programmes. Merit scholarships can cover 50 to 100 percent of tuition, and there are need-based awards plus scholarships for olympiad and sporting talent.
documents: Secondary school or bachelor's degree with transcript and certified translation
Proof of English proficiency (IELTS 6.5+ or TOEFL iBT 90+)
References, an online test or an interview, if required
kozminski.metaDescription: Kozminski University, Warsaw: Triple Crown accredited and Poland's leading private university. Tuition, scholarships and entry deadlines. Free assessment.

europea.intro: Spain's leading private university, with campuses in Madrid, Valencia, Alicante and the Canary Islands. Over 40 percent of students come from abroad, from more than 110 countries.
europea.reputation: The university builds its teaching around a learning-by-doing model — practical work, simulations and real projects. A simulated hospital, laboratories and production studios are part of everyday teaching. Eighty-eight percent of graduates find work within 18 months. The partnership with Real Madrid Graduate School gives its sports programmes a unique standing in Europe, and strong industry links secure work placements.
highlights: Partnership with Real Madrid Graduate School for sports programmes
88 percent of graduates employed within 18 months
A simulated hospital, laboratories and production studios on campus
Over 40 percent international students from more than 110 countries
europea.campus: The Madrid campus is large and green, with sports centres and a simulated hospital; Valencia and Alicante are urban and central, while the Canary Islands campuses are sunny and tourism-focused. All are equipped with laboratories, libraries, cafés and sports facilities. University residences start at 600 euros a month, and shared flats range from 400 to 800 euros, with another 500 to 800 euros for other costs.
europea.admissions: Admissions are rolling, with the main intake in September/October and a February intake for some programmes. Bachelor's tuition ranges from 10,000 to 18,000 euros per year and master's from 12,000 to 21,000 euros in total. Merit scholarships offer up to 50 percent off, alongside sports scholarships, support for international students and family discounts. Early applications are given priority.
documents: Secondary school or bachelor's degree with certified translation and transcript
Proof of English proficiency (IELTS 6.0+, TOEFL or the university's own test)
Motivation letter, CV and references (for master's programmes)
An interview or entrance test, if required
